nodes.description: Part of the emergency protocol: intravenous glucose and lipids to prevent catabolism during febrile illness.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent acute liver failure due to NBAS deficiency: phenotypic spectrum, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic concepts.
evidence.snippet: Antipyretic therapy and induction of anabolism including glucose and parenteral lipids effectively ameliorates the course of liver crises.

evidence.reference_title: NBAS deficiency due to biallelic c.2809C > G variant presenting with recurrent acute liver failure with severe hyperammonemia, acquired microcephaly and progressive brain atrophy.
evidence.snippet: An early and consequent administration of antipyretics together with an anabolic energy management (high glucose and lipids) proved to be highly beneficial on liver function recovery but it seems to have no effect on the course of CNS involvement.

nodes.description: Apoptosis of NBAS-deficient cells at febrile temperature, measured by flow cytometry in patient fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Biallelic germline variants in NBAS at 2p24.3. The allelic series is large and mostly private: missense, nonsense, frameshift, canonical and deep intronic splice variants, and exon deletions have all been reported. In the 110-patient cohort, missense variants and in-frame deletions in the Sec39 domain defined the ILFS2 subgroup. In China, c.3596G>A (p.Cys1199Tyr) is a recurrent allele strongly associated with the liver-failure phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic Mutations in NBAS Cause Recurrent Acute Liver Failure with Onset in Infancy.
evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing in five unrelated individuals with fever-dependent RALF revealed biallelic mutations in NBAS.

evidence.reference_title: Defining clinical subgroups and genotype-phenotype correlations in NBAS-associated disease across 110 patients.
evidence.snippet: three clinical subgroups arise that differ significantly regarding main clinical features and are directly related to the affected region of the NBAS protein: β-propeller (combined phenotype), Sec39 (infantile liver failure syndrome type 2/ILFS2), and C-terminal (short stature, optic atrophy, and Pelger-Huët anomaly/SOPH)

evidence.reference_title: [Clinical features and genetic study of four cases of pediatric acute liver failure caused by NBAS gene variants].
evidence.snippet: The c.3596G>A variant site is a hotspot mutation in China and is strongly correlated with the liver failure phenotype.

nodes.description: Part of the emergency protocol: start antipyretics as soon as fever begins. The 230-patient study recommends metamizole, because ibuprofen raises bleeding risk when liver function is impaired and paracetamol toxicity produces reactive oxygen species, which may contribute to the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent acute liver failure due to NBAS deficiency: phenotypic spectrum, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic concepts.
evidence.snippet: Antipyretic therapy and induction of anabolism including glucose and parenteral lipids effectively ameliorates the course of liver crises.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic Phenotype in NBAS-Associated Disease: Clinical Course, Prognostic Factors and Outcome in 230 Patients.
evidence.snippet: For antipyretic therapy, we recommend metamizole (8–16 mg/kg body weight as a single dose orally or parenterally at minimum intervals of 6 h, maximum single dose: 1000 mg), considering the increased risk of bleeding when using ibuprofen in the context of impaired liver function and the fact that paracetamol toxicity induces reactive oxidative species, which might play a role in the pathogenesis of the disease

nodes.description: Fever during infection is the trigger of liver crises, not a cause of the disease. Other reported triggers include the postnatal catabolic period, fever after vaccination, surgery and chemotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic Phenotype in NBAS-Associated Disease: Clinical Course, Prognostic Factors and Outcome in 230 Patients.
evidence.snippet: Febrile infections were reported as a trigger of liver crises in all but one affected patient.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic Phenotype in NBAS-Associated Disease: Clinical Course, Prognostic Factors and Outcome in 230 Patients.
evidence.snippet: In addition to febrile infections, reported triggers were postnatal catabolic period, fever post‐vaccination, chemotherapy, surgery, difficult intravenous sampling or catheterization, cold or hot temperatures, long‐distance travel, and the end of interferon therapy.

nodes.description: Hepatic encephalopathy accompanied liver crises in about 90% of the ILFS2 subgroup, with a median grade of III.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic Phenotype in NBAS-Associated Disease: Clinical Course, Prognostic Factors and Outcome in 230 Patients.

evidence.snippet: Steatosis was reported in 85% of cases (n = 52) and necrosis in 54% (n = 37) while disturbances of liver architecture and cirrhosis were not found.

nodes.description: Death of hepatocytes during a febrile crisis, reflected in transaminase activities in the thousands and in hepatocyte necrosis on biopsy. Hepatocytes are proposed to be especially vulnerable because of their high secretory load.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of vesicular trafficking presenting with recurrent acute liver failure: NBAS, RINT1, and SCYL1 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The impairment of protein secretion by compromised antegrade transport provides a possible explanation for different organ manifestations such as bone alteration due to lack of collagens or diabetes mellitus when insulin secretion is affected.

nodes.description: Independently of its trafficking role, NBAS recruits the core NMD factor UPF1 to the ER membrane and, with UPF1, controls the stability of ER-associated transcripts, especially stress-response transcripts. Nbas knockdown in zebrafish embryos impairs degradation of PTC-containing mRNAs. Whether loss of this function contributes to ILFS2 is unknown.

animal_models.description: Shows that Nbas depletion impairs degradation of PTC-containing mRNAs in vivo.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a localized nonsense-mediated decay pathway at the endoplasmic reticulum.
evidence.snippet: NBAS and UPF1 coregulate the stability of ER-associated transcripts, in particular those associated with the cellular stress response.

evidence.reference_title: Dhx34 and Nbas function in the NMD pathway and are required for embryonic development in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: We also found that Dhx34 and Nbas are required for degradation of PTC-containing mRNAs in zebrafish embryos.

nodes.description: NBAS links p31 to the ZW10-RINT1 subcomplex, which tethers COPI vesicles returning from the Golgi to the ER. Depleting NBAS in cultured cells redistributes Golgi recycling proteins and causes a protein glycosylation defect, and patient fibroblasts show disturbed vesicle tethering. The 2025 review proposes that impaired retrograde transport also impairs membrane recycling and autophagy.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of the neuroblastoma-amplified gene product as a component of the syntaxin 18 complex implicated in Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde transport.
evidence.snippet: NAG depletion did not substantially affect Golgi morphology and protein export from the ER, but it caused redistribution of Golgi recycling proteins accompanied by a defect in protein glycosylation.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of vesicular trafficking presenting with recurrent acute liver failure: NBAS, RINT1, and SCYL1 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Dysfunction of retrograde transport impairs membrane recycling and autophagy.
